subject: Linguistics
title: Clipping and Abbreviation
description: A 60-second lesson on Clipping and Abbreviation.

hook.text: 'Phone' came from 'telephone,' 'flu' from 'influenza.' We love cutting words short.

buildup.text: Clipping removes part of a word while keeping the same meaning and part of speech.

discovery.text: Back-clipping is most common (exam ← examination), but front-clipping exists too (bus ← omnibus).

twist.text: Acronyms start as abbreviations but become words themselves—'scuba' and 'laser' are examples.

climax.text: Once clipped, the short form often replaces the original—nobody says 'omnibus' anymore.

punchline.text: Long words shrink—and the short version wins.

quiz.question: What is back-clipping?
options: Removing the end of a word
